question: How many fundamental duties were recommended to be inserted in the Indian Constitution by the Swarna Singh Committee?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Swaran Singh Committee (1976), headed by Sardar Swaran Singh, was constituted to recommend the incorporation of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution. (स्वर्ण सिंह समिति — 8 कर्तव्यों की सिफारिश)

 

• The Committee recommended that 8 Fundamental Duties be added to the Constitution.

 

• Acting on this, the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 actually inserted 10 Fundamental Duties (via new Article 51-A in a new Part IV-A) — the government added two more duties than the committee had recommended, while dropping the committee's suggestion on payment of taxes.

 

• A further duty (the 11th, on parents/guardians providing educational opportunities to children) was added later by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, making the present total 11 Fundamental Duties.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Russia).

 

• Fundamental Duties are not justiciable, i.e., not enforceable by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights.

 

NOTE

 

• 7, 6 and 9 (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these matches the number of duties actually recommended by the Swaran Singh Committee, which was 8.

question: Parkash Singh Badal passed away in April 2023. He served as Chief Minister of _______ for five times.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Parkash Singh Badal was a veteran leader of the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and served as the Chief Minister of Punjab five times — the longest-serving CM of the state. (प्रकाश सिंह बादल — पंजाब के मुख्यमंत्री)

 

• He passed away on 25 April 2023 at the age of 95.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (India's second-highest civilian award) in 2015.

 

• His son, Sukhbir Singh Badal, has also served as Deputy Chief Minister and later President of the Shiromani Akali Dal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Parkash Singh Badal was also the youngest Chief Minister of Punjab when he first took office in 1970.

 

• He is the father-in-law of Harsimrat Kaur Badal, a former Union Minister.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar, Himachal Pradesh and Haryana (Options 1, 3 and 4): Parkash Singh Badal never served as Chief Minister of any of these states; his entire political career as CM was in Punjab.

question: Dussehra festival is celebrated in which of the following Hindu months?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ashwin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dussehra (Vijayadashami) is celebrated on the tenth day (Dashami) of the bright fortnight (Shukla Paksha) of the Hindu month of Ashwin. (दशहरा — अश्विन मास)

 

• It marks the culmination of the nine-day Navratri festival and symbolises the victory of good over evil.

 

• The festival commemorates Lord Rama's victory over Ravana as well as Goddess Durga's victory over the demon Mahishasura.

 

• In the Gregorian calendar, Ashwin typically falls in September-October.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ravan Dahan (burning of effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnad) is a key ritual associated with Dussehra celebrations across North India.

 

• The Hindu lunar calendar has twelve months: Chaitra, Vaisakha, Jyeshtha, Ashadha, Shravana, Bhadrapada, Ashwin, Kartika, Margashirsha, Pausha, Magha and Phalguna.

 

NOTE

 

• Chaitra (Option 1): This is the first month of the Hindu lunisolar calendar, associated with Chaitra Navratri/Ram Navami, not Dussehra.

 

• Vaisakha (Option 3): Associated with festivals like Baisakhi and Buddha Purnima, not Dussehra.

 

• Ashadha (Option 4): Associated with the Rath Yatra of Lord Jagannath, not Dussehra.

question: Which feature in MS Word allows you to see a document's layout and formatting as it will appear when printed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Print Preview.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Print Preview in MS Word shows exactly how the document's layout, margins, page breaks and formatting will look once it is printed on paper. (प्रिंट पूर्वावलोकन — मुद्रित रूप देखने की सुविधा)

 

• It allows the user to check for errors, alignment issues and overall page layout before actually printing the document, saving paper and ink.

 

• In modern versions of MS Word, Print Preview is integrated into the Print option under the File tab (Backstage view), showing the preview alongside print settings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Read Mode/Reading View optimises the document for on-screen reading rather than printing, hiding editing toolbars.

 

• Draft View shows text formatting but simplifies the page layout (no headers/footers/margins) for faster editing.

 

NOTE

 

• Draft View (Option 1): Used for quick editing; it does not show the page exactly as it will print (headers, footers, columns are hidden).

 

• Screen View (Option 2): Not a standard core MS Word view name for print layout checking.

 

• Reading View (Option 4): Optimised for comfortable on-screen reading, not for previewing the printed page layout.

question: In whose ashram did the Beatles compose rock music in 1968 influenced by classical music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharshi Mahesh Yogi Ashram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1968, the British rock band The Beatles travelled to Rishikesh, India, and stayed at the ashram of Maharishi Mahesh Yogi to study Transcendental Meditation. (महर्षि महेश योगी आश्रम, ऋषिकेश — बीटल्स)

 

• During this stay, influenced by their exposure to Indian spirituality and classical music traditions, the band composed a large number of songs, many of which appeared on The Beatles (the "White Album"), released later in 1968.

 

• The ashram is popularly known today as the "Beatles Ashram" and is located within the Rajaji National Park area near Rishikesh, Uttarakhand.

 

• George Harrison, in particular, had already been influenced by Indian classical music through his association with sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Beatles Ashram is now a heritage and tourist site, featuring meditation halls and murals related to the band's visit.

 

• Rishikesh is also known as the "Yoga Capital of the World".

 

NOTE

 

• Osho Rajnish Ashram (Option 2): Located in Pune; not connected to the Beatles' 1968 visit.

 

• Pandit Ravishankar Ashram (Option 3): Ravi Shankar was a sitar guru who influenced George Harrison musically but did not run the ashram where the Beatles stayed and composed songs in 1968.

 

• Maharshi Aurobindo Ashram (Option 4): Located in Puducherry (Pondicherry), founded by Sri Aurobindo; unrelated to the Beatles' visit.

question: What is the standard weight of hammer for women in the hammer throw event?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4 kg.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the athletics event of hammer throw, the standard weight of the hammer for women is 4 kg, while for men it is 7.26 kg (16 lb). (हैमर थ्रो — महिलाओं के लिए 4 किग्रा)

 

• The hammer consists of a metal ball attached to a grip by a steel wire.

 

• Hammer throw is a traditional track-and-field event contested at events like the Olympics and World Athletics Championships.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The women's hammer throw was added to the Olympic programme in 2000 (Sydney Olympics), much later than the men's event (1900).

 

• Similar weight-differentiated rules exist for other throwing events like shot put (women: 4 kg, men: 7.26 kg) and discus throw (women: 1 kg, men: 2 kg).

 

NOTE

 

• 6 kg, 8 kg and 5 kg (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these matches the official 4 kg weight prescribed for the women's hammer in international athletics rules.

question: Brihadiswara Temple of Tanjore was built by which of the following Chola emperors?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja Raja Chola.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Brihadeeswarar (Brihadishwara) Temple at Thanjavur (Tanjore), Tamil Nadu, was built by the Chola emperor Raja Raja Chola I between 1003 and 1010 CE. (बृहदेश्वर मंदिर, तंजावुर — राजराज चोल प्रथम)

 

• It is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture, famed for its massive vimana (tower), one of the tallest in the world at the time of its construction.

 

• The temple is also known as "Rajarajeswaram", named after its builder.

 

• It is part of the "Great Living Chola Temples" UNESCO World Heritage Site, along with the Brihadeeswarar Temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram and the Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The temple is built almost entirely of granite and was constructed without any binding material such as mortar.

 

• A famous inscription in the temple records the details of its construction and administration.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajendra I (Option 1): Son and successor of Raja Raja Chola I; he founded the new capital of Gangaikonda Cholapuram and built a similar temple there.

 

• Vijayalaya (Option 3): The founder of the imperial Chola dynasty in the 9th century CE, much before the Brihadeeswarar Temple was built.

 

• Chamunda Raya (Option 4): A Ganga dynasty minister/general known for commissioning the Gomateshwara statue at Shravanabelagola, unrelated to the Cholas.

question: In which of the following years did the Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act come into force?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2015.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act, 2015 gave effect to the Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) between India and Bangladesh regarding the exchange of certain enclaves. (100वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2015 — भारत-बांग्लादेश सीमा समझौता)

 

• It came into force on 1 August 2015.

 

• Under this amendment, India and Bangladesh exchanged enclaves along their border, primarily affecting the states of Assam, West Bengal, Meghalaya and Tripura.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Land Boundary Agreement was originally signed in 1974 between Indira Gandhi and Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, but was ratified and implemented decades later via this amendment.

 

• The exchange of enclaves resolved a long-standing border dispute involving over 150 enclaves.

 

NOTE

 

• 2001, 2020 and 2009 (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these is the year the 100th Amendment Act came into force; it was 2015.

question: On 12 September 2002, ISRO launched the Kalpana-1 satellite using the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle. What is the application of this satellite?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Climate & environment communication.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalpana-1 (originally called MetSat-1) was launched by ISRO on 12 September 2002 aboard the PSLV-C4 rocket, and was later renamed in honour of astronaut Kalpana Chawla. (कल्पना-1 उपग्रह — मौसम और पर्यावरण निगरानी)

 

• It was India's first dedicated meteorological satellite, built specifically for weather forecasting and monitoring of the climate/environment, such as tracking cloud patterns and cyclones.

 

• It carried a Very High Resolution Radiometer (VHRR) payload for meteorological imaging.

 

• Its data supported the India Meteorological Department (IMD) in weather prediction and disaster preparedness related to cyclones and monsoons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kalpana-1 was placed in a Geostationary Orbit.

 

• India's subsequent dedicated meteorological satellites include the INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR series.

 

NOTE

 

• Disaster management system (Option 1): While weather data indirectly aids disaster management, Kalpana-1's core purpose was meteorological/climate monitoring, not a dedicated disaster-management satellite.

 

• Earth observation (Option 3): Dedicated Earth observation (remote sensing) satellites in India belong to the separate IRS (Indian Remote Sensing) series, distinct from Kalpana-1.

 

• Planetary observation (Option 4): Planetary observation refers to missions like Chandrayaan or Mangalyaan, not a meteorological satellite like Kalpana-1.

question: Which of the following writs in Latin means ‘we command’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mandamus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mandamus is a Latin term literally meaning "we command". (मैंडेमस — हम आदेश देते हैं)

 

• It is one of the five writs under Article 32 and Article 226 of the Indian Constitution, issued by the Supreme Court and High Courts respectively.

 

• The writ of Mandamus is issued to command a public official, government body, corporation, tribunal or lower court to perform a public or statutory duty that it has failed or refused to perform.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The five constitutional writs in India are: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo-Warranto.

 

• Mandamus cannot be issued against a private individual or to enforce a purely discretionary duty.

 

NOTE

 

• Prohibition (Option 1): Means "to forbid"; issued by a higher court to a lower court/tribunal to stop it from exceeding its jurisdiction.

 

• Habeas corpus (Option 2): Means "to have the body"; issued to produce a detained person before the court to check the legality of detention.

 

• Quo-warranto (Option 3): Means "by what authority"; issued to question the legal authority of a person holding a public office.

question: What is the primary aim of Regional Rural Banks in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Development of rural economy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were established under the RRB Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Narasimham Committee (1975), with the primary aim of developing the rural economy. (क्षेत्रीय ग्रामीण बैंक — ग्रामीण अर्थव्यवस्था का विकास)

 

• The first RRB, Prathama Bank, was set up on 2 October 1975 at Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, sponsored by the Syndicate Bank.

 

• RRBs primarily provide credit and banking facilities to small farmers, agricultural labourers, artisans and small entrepreneurs in rural areas.

 

• Ownership of RRBs is jointly held by the Central Government (50%), the sponsor bank (35%) and the State Government (15%).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• RRBs function under the supervision of NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development).

 

• The Government has undertaken several rounds of amalgamation of RRBs to strengthen their financial viability.

 

NOTE

 

• Urban, semi-urban and metropolitan economy (Options 2, 3 and 4): RRBs were specifically designed to serve rural areas and the rural economy, not urban, semi-urban or metropolitan regions, which are primarily served by commercial banks.

question: In which state is the Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve is located in the state of Uttarakhand, in the Chamoli, Almora, Pithoragarh and Bageshwar districts. (नंदा देवी जीवमंडल रिज़र्व — उत्तराखंड)

 

• It encompasses the Nanda Devi National Park and the Valley of Flowers National Park, both of which together form a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

• It was designated a Biosphere Reserve in 1988 and included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2004.

 

• Nanda Devi, at 7,816 metres, is the second-highest mountain peak in India (after Kangchenjunga) and the highest located entirely within India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Valley of Flowers National Park, within this reserve, is famous for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers and diverse fauna, including the Asiatic black bear and snow leopard.

 

• Uttarakhand is also home to other important protected areas like Corbett National Park and Rajaji National Park.

 

NOTE

 

• Himachal Pradesh, Assam and Odisha (Options 2, 3 and 4): The Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve is not located in any of these states; it lies entirely within Uttarakhand.

question: Which was the first programmable general purpose computer in the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ENIAC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer) is regarded as the first programmable, general-purpose electronic digital computer in the world. (ईएनआईएसी — पहला प्रोग्रामेबल सामान्य-प्रयोजन कंप्यूटर)

 

• It was built by J. Presper Eckert and John Mauchly at the University of Pennsylvania, USA, and completed in 1945.

 

• ENIAC used vacuum tubes and was primarily designed to compute artillery firing tables for the US Army, but its general-purpose design allowed it to be reprogrammed for a wide range of computational problems.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• ENIAC weighed about 30 tons and occupied a room of around 1,800 square feet.

 

• It was later succeeded by stored-program computers like the EDVAC and EDSAC, based on the von Neumann architecture.

 

NOTE

 

• Pascaline (Option 1): A mechanical calculator invented by Blaise Pascal in 1642, capable only of addition and subtraction — not programmable or general-purpose.

 

• Napier's bones (Option 2): A manual calculating tool devised by John Napier in the early 17th century to assist multiplication and division — not an electronic or programmable device.

 

• Mark I (Option 4): An early electromechanical computer built at Harvard University (1944), predating ENIAC and generally considered less flexible/general-purpose than ENIAC.

question: Which country’s national game is Chinlone (Caneball)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Myanmar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chinlone, also known as Caneball, is the traditional national sport of Myanmar (Burma). (चिनलोन/केनबॉल — म्यांमार का राष्ट्रीय खेल)

 

• It is played with a woven rattan (cane) ball and combines elements of sport and dance, typically played by a team keeping the ball airborne using any part of the body except the hands.

 

• Chinlone is deeply rooted in Myanmar's cultural heritage and is often performed at festivals as much as it is played competitively.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• National games of neighbouring countries: Bhutan — Archery (Datse); Afghanistan — Buzkashi.

 

• Sepak Takraw, a related cane-ball sport, is popular in Southeast Asian countries like Thailand and Malaysia.

 

NOTE

 

• Afghanistan (Option 1): The national game of Afghanistan is Buzkashi, not Chinlone.

 

• Bhutan (Option 2): The national game of Bhutan is Archery, not Chinlone.

 

• China (Option 3): China does not officially recognise Chinlone as its national game; table tennis is widely regarded as China's most dominant national sport.

question: Which Act was enacted by the British which regulated the manufacture, sale, possession and transport of firearms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Arms Act, 1878.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Arms Act, 1878 was enacted by the British colonial government to regulate the manufacture, sale, possession, and transport of firearms in India. (भारतीय शस्त्र अधिनियम, 1878)

 

• It was passed in the aftermath of the Revolt of 1857, partly to prevent Indians from possessing arms and to control potential uprisings against British rule.

 

• The Act imposed strict licensing requirements on Indians for owning and carrying weapons, while exempting Europeans in many cases — making it widely criticised as discriminatory.

 

• Leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Gopal Krishna Gokhale criticised the Act for this discriminatory treatment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian Arms Act, 1878 remained in force until it was replaced by the Arms Act, 1959, post-independence.

 

• Other repressive laws of the same era include the Vernacular Press Act, 1878 and the Dramatic Performances Act, 1876.

 

NOTE

 

• The Arm Rules, 1839 (Option 2): Not a recognised historical Act by this name for regulating firearms in colonial India.

 

• The Arms Act,1857 (Option 3): No such Act was enacted in 1857; the relevant legislation came two decades later, in 1878.

 

• The Firearms Act, 1871 (Option 4): Not the correct name/year of the British-era Indian legislation on firearms; the actual law was the Indian Arms Act of 1878.

question: Which classical dance was introduced by the great Vaishnava saint and reformer of Assam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sattriya is the classical dance form introduced in the 15th century by the great Vaishnava saint and social reformer of Assam, Srimanta Sankardeva. (सत्रिया नृत्य — शंकरदेव, असम)

 

• It originated in the Sattras (Vaishnava monasteries) of Assam as a means of propagating the Bhakti movement through dance-drama performances called Ankiya Naat.

 

• Sattriya was officially recognised as one of the eight classical dance forms of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The eight classical dances of India are: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

 

• Srimanta Sankardeva also founded the Ekasarana Dharma and promoted the Bhakti movement in Assam through literature, music (Borgeet) and drama.

 

NOTE

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 1): A classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh, unrelated to Assam.

 

• Odissi (Option 2): A classical dance form of Odisha, unrelated to the Vaishnava reformer of Assam.

 

• Kathak (Option 3): A classical dance form of North India (Uttar Pradesh), not introduced by Sankardeva.

question: India hosted Men’s Hockey World Cup in 2023 at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhubaneswar and Rourkela.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2023 Men's Hockey World Cup was jointly hosted by India in the cities of Bhubaneswar and Rourkela, Odisha, from 13 to 29 January 2023. (हॉकी विश्व कप 2023 — भुवनेश्वर और राउरकेला, ओडिशा)

 

• Matches were played at the Kalinga Stadium in Bhubaneswar and the newly built Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium in Rourkela, the largest hockey stadium in the world.

 

• Germany won the tournament, defeating Belgium in the final; India finished in 9th place.

 

• This was the second consecutive time India hosted the tournament, having previously hosted it in 2018 in Bhubaneswar alone.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium in Rourkela is named after the tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda and has a seating capacity of around 20,000.

 

• Odisha has been a long-time sponsor of Indian hockey, also supporting the Indian men's and women's national hockey teams.

 

NOTE

 

• Patna and Gaya, Nashik and Nagpur, Amritsar and Bathinda (Options 2, 3 and 4): None of these city pairs hosted the 2023 Men's Hockey World Cup; the actual host cities were Bhubaneswar and Rourkela.

question: What does SAARC stand for?
option_1: South Asian Association of Regional Cartography
option_2: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
option_3: South Asian Association of Regional Climate change
option_4: South Asian Association of Regional Corporation
solution_text:
The correct answer is South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• SAARC stands for the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation. (सार्क — दक्षिण एशियाई क्षेत्रीय सहयोग संगठन)

 

• It was established on 8 December 1985 with the signing of its charter in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

 

• Its headquarters/secretariat is located in Kathmandu, Nepal.

 

• SAARC has eight member states: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan (which joined in 2007).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The idea of SAARC was first mooted by Bangladeshi President Ziaur Rahman.

 

• SAARC aims to promote economic and social development, collective self-reliance, and cooperation among South Asian nations.

 

NOTE

 

• South Asian Association of Regional Cartography, Climate change and Corporation (Options 1, 3 and 4): These are not the actual expansion of SAARC; the correct full form uses "Cooperation", not Cartography, Climate change, or Corporation.

question: The Atal Tunnel has been built by Border Road Organisation at an altitude of 3000 metres. Which places are connected by this tunnel?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manali to Lahaul-Spiti.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Atal Tunnel connects Manali in the Kullu Valley to the Lahaul-Spiti valley of Himachal Pradesh, via a tunnel under the Rohtang Pass. (अटल सुरंग — मनाली और लाहौल-स्पीति)

 

• It was built by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) and inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 3 October 2020.

 

• At the time of construction, it was the longest highway tunnel above 3,000 metres altitude in the world, spanning about 9.02 km.

 

• The tunnel reduces the road distance between Manali and Lahaul-Spiti by around 46 km and ensures all-weather connectivity, as the region was earlier cut off for nearly six months every winter due to snow at Rohtang Pass.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tunnel was originally named the Rohtang Tunnel and was later renamed the Atal Tunnel after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

 

• The tunnel is a key strategic link providing faster military access towards the Ladakh border region as well.

 

NOTE

 

• Shimla to Ladakh and Shimla to Srinagar (Options 1 and 2): The tunnel is not located on any Shimla route; it connects Manali and Lahaul-Spiti.

 

• Manali to Shimla (Option 3): The tunnel does not connect Manali to Shimla; it connects Manali to the Lahaul-Spiti valley.

question: Which type of system did the leaders of independent India decide to adopt?
option_1: A system that would promote the welfare of the government
option_2: A system that would promote the welfare of few rather than all
option_3: A system that would promote the welfare of all rather than a few
option_4: A system that would promote the welfare of private enterprises
solution_text:
The correct answer is A system that would promote the welfare of all rather than a few.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After Independence, the leaders of India resolved to establish a welfare state, adopting a system that would promote the welfare of all citizens rather than the benefit of only a select few. (कल्याणकारी राज्य — सभी का कल्याण)

 

• This vision is embodied in the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV of the Constitution), which direct the State to secure a social order for the promotion of the welfare of the people.

 

• India adopted a mixed economy model and democratic-socialist principles to reduce inequality and ensure broad-based development.

 

• Article 38 of the Constitution explicitly obligates the State to strive to promote the welfare of the people by securing a social order permeated by justice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Preamble to the Constitution also reflects this welfare orientation, resolving to secure Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity for all citizens.

 

• The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added the words "Socialist" and "Secular" to the Preamble, reinforcing this welfare orientation.

 

NOTE

 

• Welfare of the government (Option 1): India's leaders sought welfare for the people, not for the government itself.

 

• Welfare of few rather than all (Option 2): This is the opposite of the inclusive welfare vision that independent India's leaders actually adopted.

 

• Welfare of private enterprises (Option 4): India's post-independence system was aimed at public welfare broadly, not specifically favouring private enterprise.

question: The 9th Men's ICC T20 World Cup Cricket 2024 will be hosted by which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Indies and USA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 9th ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024 was jointly hosted by the West Indies and the United States of America, held from 1 to 29 June 2024. (टी20 विश्व कप 2024 — वेस्टइंडीज और अमेरिका)

 

• This was the first time the T20 World Cup was held (partly) in the USA, marking a major step in expanding cricket's reach in North America.

 

• India won the tournament, defeating South Africa in the final held at Kensington Oval, Barbados, to claim their second T20 World Cup title.

 

• Rohit Sharma captained the winning Indian team; Virat Kohli was named Player of the Match in the final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2026 T20 World Cup is scheduled to be jointly hosted by India and Sri Lanka.

 

• The inaugural T20 World Cup was held in South Africa in 2007, won by India under M.S. Dhoni.

 

NOTE

 

• Canada and USA (Option 1): Canada was not a host nation of the 2024 tournament, though it participated as a playing team.

 

• India and Sri Lanka (Option 2): This pairing refers to the upcoming 2026 T20 World Cup, not the 2024 edition.

 

• India and Bangladesh (Option 4): Neither country hosted the 2024 T20 World Cup; the actual hosts were the West Indies and USA.

question: In February 2023, PARAKH became the First National Assessment Regulator. What does R stand for in PARAKH?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Review.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• PARAKH stands for Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development — here, R stands for "Review". (परख — शिक्षा गुणवत्ता आकलन संस्था)

 

• It was set up in February 2023 by the Ministry of Education, as a constituent unit of the NCERT (National Council of Educational Research and Training).

 

• PARAKH functions as India's first National Assessment Regulator, established under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, to set norms and standards for student assessment across school boards.

 

• It aims to bring equivalence between different education boards (State, CBSE, ICSE, etc.) through common assessment frameworks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• PARAKH also conducts the National Achievement Survey (NAS) to assess learning outcomes of students at the national level.

 

• The National Education Policy 2020 emphasises holistic, competency-based assessment over rote-learning-based examinations.

 

NOTE

 

• Related, Report and Recall (Options 1, 2 and 4): None of these words is part of the official expansion of PARAKH; the correct term for "R" is "Review".

question: In which year did Wilhelm Johannsen coin the term ‘gene’ to describe the Mendelian units of heredity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1909.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Danish botanist and geneticist Wilhelm Johannsen coined the term "gene" in 1909 to describe the fundamental physical and functional unit of heredity, in his work *Elemente der exakten Erblichkeitslehre*. (जीन शब्द — विल्हेम योहानसेन, 1909)

 

• Johannsen also introduced the related terms "genotype" and "phenotype" in the same period, distinguishing an organism's genetic makeup from its observable traits.

 

• His work built upon Gregor Mendel's earlier laws of inheritance (formulated in the 1860s, rediscovered around 1900).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The physical structure of DNA (the molecule carrying genes) was later discovered by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953.

 

• Gregor Mendel is known as the "Father of Genetics" for his pioneering experiments on pea plants.

 

NOTE

 

• 1900, 1920 and 1910 (Options 2, 3 and 4): None of these is the year Johannsen coined the term "gene"; the correct year is 1909.

question: Electrochemical cell is a device which converts chemical energy into electrical energy in a/an _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is indirect redox reaction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An electrochemical cell (galvanic/voltaic cell) converts chemical energy into electrical energy through an indirect redox reaction, where oxidation and reduction occur in separate half-cells connected by a salt bridge and an external circuit. (विद्युत रासायनिक सेल — अप्रत्यक्ष रेडॉक्स अभिक्रिया)

 

• Because the oxidation half-reaction (at the anode) and reduction half-reaction (at the cathode) are physically separated, electrons must flow through an external wire to complete the circuit — this indirect transfer of electrons generates a usable electric current.

 

• This contrasts with a direct redox reaction (as in a simple beaker reaction), where oxidising and reducing agents are mixed together and electrons transfer directly without producing a usable current.

 

• A classic example is the Daniell cell, where zinc is oxidised at the anode and copper ions are reduced at the cathode.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• In an electrolytic cell, the reverse happens: electrical energy is used to drive a non-spontaneous redox reaction.

 

• The electrode potentials of half-cells are measured relative to the Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE).

 

NOTE

 

• Oxidation reaction and reduction reaction (Options 1 and 2): These describe only one half of the overall process; an electrochemical cell involves both, coupled together, not either alone.

 

• Direct redox reaction (Option 3): In a direct redox reaction, electron transfer happens without generating a controlled electric current, unlike in an electrochemical cell.

question: In classical Carnatic music, tempo is called as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is laya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Carnatic (South Indian classical) music, tempo or rhythmic speed is called "laya". (लय — कर्नाटक संगीत में गति/तेम्पो)

 

• Laya is one of the fundamental elements of Indian classical music, alongside raga (melody) and tala (rhythmic cycle).

 

• Laya is broadly classified into three types: vilambit (slow), madhya (medium) and drut (fast) tempo.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tala refers to the rhythmic framework/time cycle in Indian classical music, measured through a fixed pattern of beats.

 

• Famous Carnatic music composers include Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri, collectively known as the "Trinity of Carnatic Music".

 

NOTE

 

• Gita (Option 1): Refers to a simple melodic song form used as a beginner's lesson in Carnatic music, not tempo.

 

• Achala (Option 3): Not a standard Carnatic music term for tempo.

 

• Padam (Option 4): A slow-tempo, expressive musical composition form in Carnatic music (often on themes of love/devotion), not the term for tempo itself.
